Ticket Id: 7715

Dr Grantley Gross
Consultant Endocrinologist
City Hospital, Siute 32
55 Main Road
Newtown.

24/01/15

Dear Dr. Gross,

Re: Mr. Brett Collister, DOB: 20/11/1970

I am writing to refer to you Mr. Collister, a 45-year- old factory foreman who has signs and symptoms
suggestive of Diabetes Mellitus Type 2. He is married with 3 children aged 18, 16 and 13. He had a past
history of infectious mononucleosis in January 2013.

Initially, Mr. Collister presented to me on 22/03/14 complaining of a sore throat and a productive cough
with green phlegm over the previous week. He showed no improvement on his next visit on 26/05/14 with
inflamed tonsils and fever. Therefore, Amoxicillin was prescribed. Three months later, he experienced pain
in his left shoulder while playing a game of darts. Keeping in mind the possibility of a rotator cuff tear, I
commenced him on Ibuprofen and referred him to a physiotherapist. It is worthy to note that he suffered
an intermittent unexplained right knee pain on 26/10/14.

Mr. Collister attended my clinic on 04/01/15 after he had felt dizzy over the previous three weeks.
Examination was normal apart from being overweight (BMI was 29.7) and unfit. Regrettably, he started to
have a decreased aquity of vision combined with sore eyes three weeks later. Blood tests revealed
elevated both fasting and random blood glucose in addition to elevated HDL/LDL ratio.

I would greatly appreciate your further assessment and management of this patient.

Yours sincerely,

Dr. X
